subject: Chemistry
central_question: How did experimental evidence lead from early atomic models to the quantum-mechanical description of electrons?
in_scope_units: Discovery of electron, proton, and neutron.
Electromagnetic radiation, quantisation, photoelectric effect, and spectra.
Dual nature, uncertainty, orbitals, and quantum numbers.

known_pitfalls.claim: An orbit and an orbital are identical.
known_pitfalls.correction: An orbit is a fixed Bohr path; an orbital is a probability distribution.
Classical orbiting electrons would radiate energy, so stability remained unexplained.

known_pitfalls.claim: Uncertainty is caused only by poor instruments.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is a fundamental quantum limit.
Three p orbitals together hold six electrons.
Orbital energies can reorder after occupation.

ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use exercises on subatomic particles, radiation, photoelectric effect, Bohr transitions, de Broglie wavelength, quantum numbers, and configurations.
